linear-algebra.q: Two states satisfy ⟨u|v⟩ = 0. What does that tell you?
options: They are orthogonal — perfectly distinguishable by some measurement
They differ only by a global phase
linear-algebra.why: A zero inner product means orthogonality, and orthogonal states can be distinguished with certainty by measuring in a basis that contains them.

linear-algebra.q: The eigenvalues of a Hermitian operator are always…
linear-algebra.why: Hermitian operators have real eigenvalues — that is why observables are Hermitian. Only special ones (like the Paulis) have eigenvalues ±1.

complex-numbers-dirac-notation.q: How is the bra ⟨ψ| related to the ket |ψ⟩?
options: It is the same vector written backwards
It is the complex conjugate of each amplitude, kept as a column
complex-numbers-dirac-notation.why: ⟨ψ| = (|ψ⟩)† — transpose the column into a row and complex-conjugate each amplitude.

complex-numbers-dirac-notation.q: How do |ψ⟩ and e^{iθ}|ψ⟩ differ physically?
options: Not at all — a global phase is unobservable
They differ only when θ = π
complex-numbers-dirac-notation.why: All probabilities are |amplitude|², so a global phase cancels in every prediction. Only relative phases between components matter.

quantum-mechanics-basics.q: What does measuring a qubit in the Z basis do to the state α|0⟩ + β|1⟩?
options: Reads out α and β without disturbance
Projects it onto |0⟩ or |1⟩ and destroys the superposition
Rotates it by a random angle
quantum-mechanics-basics.why: Measurement projects onto an outcome with Born-rule probabilities |α|² and |β|², destroying the amplitudes you did not observe.

quantum-mechanics-basics.q: Why can't an error-correcting code just measure its data qubits to find errors?
options: Direct measurement would collapse the encoded superposition
Errors are too small to see
quantum-mechanics-basics.why: Reading the data destroys the very state being protected. QEC instead measures parities (stabilizers) via ancillas, which reveal errors without revealing the data.

qubits-pauli-operators.q: What is the algebraic relation between Pauli X and Z on the same qubit?
options: They are equal up to phase
They are inverses of each other
qubits-pauli-operators.why: XZ = −ZX. This anticommutation is the engine of QEC: a stabilizer flips sign exactly when an error anticommutes with it.

qubits-pauli-operators.q: Up to phase, the Pauli Y equals…
qubits-pauli-operators.why: Y = iXZ — a bit flip and a phase flip together. That is why a Y error triggers both X-type and Z-type stabilizers.

quantum-gates-circuits.q: An X error hits the control qubit just before a CNOT. What comes out?
options: X on both control and target
quantum-gates-circuits.why: CNOT copies X errors from control to target (and Z errors from target to control). Error propagation through CNOTs is why circuit design matters for fault tolerance.

quantum-gates-circuits.q: What does the Hadamard gate do to |0⟩?
quantum-gates-circuits.why: H exchanges the Z and X bases: |0⟩ ↔ |+⟩, |1⟩ ↔ |−⟩. It is how circuits switch between measuring Z-type and X-type information.

classical-error-correction.q: The 3-bit repetition code (0→000, 1→111) can correct how many bit flips?
classical-error-correction.why: Majority vote fixes any single flip. Two flips fool the vote — the codewords are distance 3 apart, and a distance-d code corrects ⌊(d−1)/2⌋ errors.

classical-error-correction.q: What does a parity check on a set of bits reveal?
options: Whether an even or odd number of those bits flipped
classical-error-correction.why: A parity check exposes only the XOR of the set — error information without reading the data. Stabilizer measurements are the quantum version of exactly this idea.

stabilizer-formalism.q: S is a stabilizer of |ψ⟩. What equation holds?
stabilizer-formalism.why: A stabilizer leaves the state exactly unchanged, eigenvalue +1. An error that anticommutes with S flips the measured value to −1 — that flip is the syndrome.

stabilizer-formalism.q: A stabilizer code on n physical qubits encoding k logical qubits has how many independent stabilizer generators?
stabilizer-formalism.why: Each independent generator halves the space; n − k generators leave 2^k dimensions — the logical subspace. The surface code: n = d², k = 1, so d²−1 stabilizers.

quantum-codes-basics.q: In the [[n, k, d]] notation, what is d?
options: The minimum weight of an undetectable logical error
quantum-codes-basics.why: d (code distance) is the smallest number of physical errors that can silently implement a logical operation. It sets how many errors are correctable: ⌊(d−1)/2⌋.

quantum-codes-basics.q: A CSS code is built from…
options: Two classical linear codes, one for X checks and one for Z checks
A single quantum code repeated twice
quantum-codes-basics.why: Calderbank–Shor–Steane codes import classical coding theory twice over: one classical code handles bit flips, another handles phase flips. The surface code is CSS.

fault-tolerance-thresholds.q: What does the threshold theorem promise when the physical error rate is below p_th?
options: Growing the code suppresses logical error rates arbitrarily far
fault-tolerance-thresholds.why: Below threshold, each increase in code distance multiplies logical error suppression — reliability becomes a matter of size, not luck. Above threshold, bigger codes make things worse.

options: A single component fault can cause at most a correctable amount of damage
fault-tolerance-thresholds.why: The circuits that extract syndromes are themselves noisy, so they must be designed to keep one fault from spreading into an uncorrectable error — via gate ordering, flags, and repetition.

topological-order-anyons.q: What determines the outcome of braiding two anyons around each other?
options: The exact shape and speed of the paths
Only the topology of the world-lines — how they wind
The distance between them at the end
topological-order-anyons.why: Path details do not matter; only the winding pattern does. That path-independence is why topological operations are naturally robust to local noise.

topological-order-anyons.q: In a topologically ordered system, the ground-state degeneracy depends on…
options: The topology (genus) of the surface it lives on
topological-order-anyons.why: On a sphere the toric code has one ground state; on a torus, four. Information stored in that degeneracy is invisible to any local observable — the essence of topological protection.

toric-code.q: How many logical qubits does the toric code on a torus encode?
toric-code.why: A torus has two independent non-contractible loops, giving two anticommuting logical operator pairs — two logical qubits, regardless of lattice size.

toric-code.q: The e and m excitations of the toric code appear at…
options: Violated vertex (star) and plaquette stabilizers — the endpoints of error strings
The corners of the lattice only
toric-code.why: Z-error strings end on violated stars (e anyons), X-error strings on violated plaquettes (m anyons). Errors make particle pairs; decoding means re-annihilating them correctly.

surface-code.q: Why is the surface code the leading candidate for real hardware?
options: It needs the fewest qubits of any code
It only requires nearest-neighbor gates on a 2D grid and tolerates ~1% error rates
It corrects unlimited errors at any rate
surface-code.why: Planar connectivity matches real chips, and its ~1% circuit-level threshold is the highest of any practical scheme — a combination no competitor matches.

surface-code.q: A rotated surface-code patch of distance d uses how many data qubits?
surface-code.why: The rotated layout needs exactly d² data qubits (plus d²−1 ancillas) — half the unrotated footprint, which is why experiments use it.

syndrome-extraction-circuits.q: How does an ancilla measure a stabilizer without touching the logical state?
options: It swaps with a data qubit
It is entangled with the neighboring data qubits via CNOTs, then measured
It measures each data qubit directly
It applies the stabilizer as a gate
syndrome-extraction-circuits.why: The CNOTs write the joint parity onto the ancilla; measuring the ancilla reveals the stabilizer value while the data superposition survives.

syndrome-extraction-circuits.q: Why does the ORDER of the four CNOTs in a stabilizer measurement matter?
options: A bad order lets ancilla faults become 'hook errors' that can halve the code distance
syndrome-extraction-circuits.why: A mid-circuit ancilla fault propagates into two data errors. With a bad schedule those align with a logical operator (a hook error); good schedules — N/Z-shaped, or diagonal 'off-the-hook' — keep them harmless.

decoding-mwpm.q: Minimum-weight perfect matching pairs up what?
options: Detection events (syndrome flips), reconstructing likely error chains
decoding-mwpm.why: Errors form chains whose endpoints light up detectors. MWPM connects those endpoints (or the boundary) with the shortest total chains — the most likely explanation under independent noise.

decoding-mwpm.q: When does decoding produce a LOGICAL error?
options: When error + correction together form a chain crossing the lattice
When more than one defect appears
decoding-mwpm.why: The correction always clears the syndrome. Failure is silent: if the guessed chain plus the real one wraps boundary to boundary, the code has applied a logical operator without knowing it.

defects-braiding.q: In defect-based computation, what is a 'hole'?
options: A manufacturing defect in the chip
A region where stabilizer measurements are switched off, creating a movable logical qubit
defects-braiding.why: Disabling stabilizers punches a hole whose boundary hosts a new logical degree of freedom. Moving and braiding holes around each other enacts logical gates.

defects-braiding.q: Why did lattice surgery largely replace braiding in modern architectures?
options: Braiding needs large holes and long schedules — far more qubits and time
defects-braiding.why: Defect braiding costs circumference-scale holes and long move sequences. Merging and splitting compact patches achieves the same gates with much less spacetime volume.

lattice-surgery.q: What does merging two surface-code patches along a boundary do?
options: Measures a joint logical operator (e.g. Z⊗Z)
Copies one qubit onto the other
lattice-surgery.why: The merged patch's new stabilizers multiply up to the joint logical Z⊗Z (or X⊗X), measuring it fault-tolerantly. Merge–split sequences build CNOTs and any Pauli-product measurement.

lattice-surgery.q: Why is lattice surgery the dominant paradigm for fault-tolerant computation?
options: It is planar, local, and space-efficient — an algorithm becomes patch layout and scheduling
lattice-surgery.why: Everything stays on a 2D grid with nearest-neighbor operations, and computation reduces to a scheduling problem — exactly what compilers can optimize.

cluster-states-mbqc.q: How does measurement-based quantum computation compute?
options: By unitary gates applied in sequence
By adaptive single-qubit measurements consuming a pre-entangled cluster state
By cooling to the ground state
cluster-states-mbqc.why: All entanglement is prepared up front; each measurement steers the remaining state, with later bases adapted to earlier outcomes.

cluster-states-mbqc.q: What connects MBQC to the surface code?
options: Unfolding a surface-code computation through time yields exactly a 3D cluster-state scheme
MBQC replaces the need for error correction
cluster-states-mbqc.why: The Raussendorf construction: stacking syndrome rounds in time gives a 3D cluster state whose measurement pattern IS surface-code fault tolerance. Two languages, one physics.

magic-states-distillation.q: Why do surface codes need magic states at all?
options: Because non-Clifford gates like T cannot be applied transversally — the state is consumed by teleportation to enact T
magic-states-distillation.why: Cliffords are cheap on the code, but Clifford-only circuits are classically simulable. The missing non-Clifford power is injected by consuming a prepared |T⟩ state via gate teleportation.

magic-states-distillation.q: What does a distillation factory do?
options: Turns many noisy magic-state copies into fewer, much cleaner ones
Removes the need for T gates
magic-states-distillation.why: 15-to-1 and similar protocols consume many rough injected states and output a few with quadratically (or better) suppressed error — historically the dominant cost of fault-tolerant algorithms.

flag-fault-tolerance.q: What event does a flag qubit 'raise' to report?
options: A data qubit left the chip
A fault inside the extraction circuit that may have spread into a dangerous correlated error
The end of a syndrome round
flag-fault-tolerance.why: The flag is entangled so that exactly the dangerous mid-circuit ancilla faults flip it. The decoder then knows to treat this round's syndrome differently and can correct the spread error.

flag-fault-tolerance.q: The main appeal of flag schemes is…
options: Higher thresholds than any other method
Fault tolerance with very few extra qubits — crucial for small devices
flag-fault-tolerance.why: One or two flag qubits replace the large verified ancilla blocks of older schemes, making fault-tolerant extraction affordable when every qubit counts.

options: A linear map, as a network of Z- and X-spiders that can be rewritten graphically
zx-calculus-basics.why: Spiders fuse and commute by a small set of complete rewrite rules, letting you simplify or verify circuits by picture-reasoning that is fully rigorous.

zx-calculus-basics.q: Why do TQEC compilers care about ZX-calculus?
options: Lattice surgery operations mirror ZX structure, so diagrams can be simplified then laid out as patches and merges
zx-calculus-basics.why: A merge is a spider fusion in disguise. Compilers like TopoLS simplify the ZX-diagram first, then translate it into a space-time layout — saving real overhead.

advanced-decoding.q: What makes the union-find decoder attractive versus MWPM?
options: It runs in almost-linear time with close-to-MWPM accuracy
advanced-decoding.why: Union-find grows and merges clusters with near-linear-time data structures, trading a little accuracy for the speed that real-time operation demands.

advanced-decoding.q: Why do plain matching decoders lose accuracy on Y-type noise?
options: They decode X and Z syndromes independently, ignoring that Y errors correlate the two
Y errors have no syndrome endpoints
advanced-decoding.why: A Y error is a correlated X-and-Z event. Decoders that exploit the correlation (reweighting one matching using the other) measurably outperform independent decoding.

options: If decoding runs slower than syndrome generation, undecoded data piles up exponentially
real-time-decoding-control.why: A superconducting device emits a syndrome round every ~1 µs, forever. A decoder that averages even slightly slower falls behind at a compounding rate — throughput is a hard constraint.

real-time-decoding-control.q: Where does real-time decoding hardware typically live?
options: On FPGAs/ASICs physically near the cryostat
Inside the dilution refrigerator's mixing chamber
real-time-decoding-control.why: Latency budgets (feed-forward for non-Clifford gates) and wiring limits push decoders into dedicated classical hardware co-located with the quantum processor.

magic-state-cultivation.q: How does cultivation differ from distillation?
options: It grows a high-fidelity magic state directly inside the code, instead of purifying many noisy copies in a factory
magic-state-cultivation.why: Cultivation prepares and checks the |T⟩ state in place on a small code, then grows the code around it — cutting the spacetime cost of magic dramatically.

magic-state-cultivation.q: Why did cultivation reshape resource estimates so sharply?
options: It made qubits cheaper to build
Magic-state production dominated the cost of fault-tolerant algorithms — shrinking it shrinks the whole machine
It removed the need for decoding
magic-state-cultivation.why: Distillation factories consumed most of the qubits in older architectures. Cutting the largest line item changes every whole-machine estimate downstream.

tqec-compilers-automation.q: What does a TQEC compiler ultimately output?
options: Machine code for a classical CPU
A space-time layout of lattice-surgery operations — patches, merges, and splits scheduled on a grid
A list of physical qubit frequencies
tqec-compilers-automation.why: From Clifford+T input, the pipeline (à la Litinski) commutes Cliffords away, leaving Pauli-product measurements laid out as 3D space-time blocks with magic-state factories placed and routed.

tqec-compilers-automation.q: In Litinski's framework, what happens to the Clifford gates?
options: They are commuted to the end and absorbed into measurement bases — never executed on hardware
They are converted to T gates
tqec-compilers-automation.why: Pushing Cliffords past the Pauli-product rotations changes which Paulis get measured, leaving only ~T-count many operations that cost actual spacetime.

clifford-simulation-hybrid.q: What does the Gottesman–Knill theorem say?
options: Circuits of only Clifford gates can be simulated efficiently on a classical computer
clifford-simulation-hybrid.why: Tracking the stabilizer group takes polynomial resources — which is exactly why Clifford-heavy QEC circuits can be validated at scale, and why non-Clifford gates are where quantum advantage hides.

clifford-simulation-hybrid.q: How do hybrid simulators like Clifft handle a few non-Clifford gates?
options: They carry a Clifford frame and factorize the small residual statevector, staying exact over billions of shots
clifford-simulation-hybrid.why: The Clifford part rides in a frame; only the non-Clifford residue needs statevector treatment, and factorizing it keeps circuits tractable that brute force could never touch.

below-threshold-experiments.q: What did Google's 2024 experiment demonstrate for the first time?
options: That growing code distance on real hardware suppresses logical error — d=7 beat d=5 beat d=3
below-threshold-experiments.why: Logical error fell by a factor Λ ≈ 2.1 per distance step — the compounding, below-threshold behavior the field had chased since the theory was written.

below-threshold-experiments.q: What does the suppression factor Λ measure?
options: The number of qubits per chip
How much the logical error rate drops when the distance increases by 2
below-threshold-experiments.why: Λ = ε_L(d) / ε_L(d+2). Λ > 1 means error correction is winning; the further above 1, the fewer qubits you need for a target logical error rate.
